object_description: two comb-like building volumes linked by a central wing
design_condition: The compact ensemble occupies the centre of the site and uses a western access square and a future eastern extension, but its deep narrow courtyards weaken the surrounding public spaces.

positive.statement: The compact volume integrates well into the existing district.
The reserved solution allows a structured and clear division of the room program.
The arrangement allows all work and teaching units to receive daylight.
The central connection provides essential links and short routes through the complex.
The architectural expression meets the expectations for this type of building.
The placement and increased height could give the multifunctional hall identification and singularity.
The structural concept appears to have been well managed.

negative.statement: The street squares are difficult to imagine as lounge areas and the shown design does not contribute sufficient quality.
The entrance is somewhat hidden behind the multifunctional hall.
The courtyards are too deep and narrow to support the desired living areas.
The reserved volume does not fully establish the independent character expected of the campus.
The quality of access and meeting spaces between teaching areas is not convincing overall.
The vertical beam arrangement makes flexible use of the spaces difficult.
The underground connection to the adjacent parking is not yet convincing.
The proposed extension connected by first-floor walkways is insufficient.
The simple spatial structure lacks spatial experiences and does not fully exploit its potential.
